alerts.title: Missing eGFR monitoring for TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines require eGFR monitoring before TDF initiation, at 3 months, 6 months, and then 6-12 monthly thereafter. The patient is on TDF and has hypertension, which is a high-risk factor for renal impairment. The current plan does not include scheduling the next eGFR test. While the latest creatinine of 112 umol/L is within normal limits, regular monitoring is mandated, especially with a comorbidity.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule eGFR monitoring as per guideline: 6-12 monthly for patients on TDF, especially with hypertension.

alerts.title: Suboptimal BP control and plan gap
alerts.message: Patient's blood pressure is 146/94 mmHg, indicating suboptimal control. He admits to missing doses of amlodipine. The guideline notes amlodipine can cause lower limb edema (1-10%) as a common side effect. The current plan only refills amlodipine without addressing adherence barriers or considering intensification of therapy. Poorly controlled hypertension increases cardiovascular risk and can exacerbate renal issues, especially while on TDF.

evidence.recommended_action: Address antihypertensive adherence, consider therapy intensification, and monitor for amlodipine side effects like edema.

alerts.title: Compounding renal risk: TDF, HTN, NSAID
alerts.message: The patient has multiple compounding risks for renal impairment: 1) Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) can cause renal failure and tubular wasting. 2) He has hypertension, a stated high-risk factor for TDF toxicity. 3) He uses ibuprofen (an NSAID) as needed, which is nephrotoxic. Trace proteinuria is present. Guidelines advise extra vigilance for renal function in TDF patients with intercurrent illness or dehydration, though none is currently reported. The combination significantly elevates risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess renal risk comprehensively; consider minimizing NSAID use and ensure strict BP control. Monitor eGFR closely.
